lines.text: Many learners say: I often think on my family.
Better: I often think about my family.
About! I often think about my family.

data.wrong: I often think on my family.
data.right: I often think about my family.

native.tip: Im Deutschen sagen wir „denken an“, darum sagen viele „on“. Im Englischen heißt es „think about“.
native.caption: Sagen Sie „think on“? 💭 Falsch: “I often think on my family.” Richtig: “I often think about my family.” Hören Sie Carlos zu und sprechen Sie nach! Mehr üben in der Lexkite-App.
native.comment: Lösung: “about”. Richtig heißt es: “I often think about my family.” Sagen Sie den Satz laut oder schreiben Sie einen eigenen Satz dazu. Üben Sie mit einem kostenlosen Quiz: {link}

en.tip: German says “denken an”, so many say “think on”. In English you say “think about”.
en.caption: German “an” is not “on” here! Wrong: “I often think on my family.” Right: “I often think about my family.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
